For parents and carers

Is this course right for my child?

Honest answers, with sources. You do not need to know anything about coding to help your child succeed here.

What the research says

The evidence for learning to code, what is strong, what is mixed and what we do not know yet. Every claim has a source.

The information-evening slides

View the slides, or download the deck and a one-page summary to print.

Questions and answers

Too young? Too much screen time? Will AI make this pointless? Short, straight answers.

What it asks of you each week

  • Sessions: one 60-minute session a week, up to 4 children, working in 2 pairs.
  • Length: each level takes 10–12 weeks; all three take 30–36 weeks. You choose, level by level, whether to continue.
  • Homework: 15–20 minutes a week, optional but encouraged. Every set has a Core task for everyone, with optional Challenge and Creative extras.
  • Equipment: a Mac, the free Scratch app and Thonny; no accounts, no internet during lessons.

How you can help at home

No coding needed. These small habits matter more than any technical knowledge:

  • Ask for a demo: “Show me what you made.”

  • Ask about the bug, not the score: “What went wrong? How did you find it?”

  • Praise strategies and effort, not “being a natural.”

  • Protect 15 minutes a week for homework, at a regular time.

  • Encourage everyone equally: girls hear less encouragement than boys.

  • Come to the showcase at the end of each level.

How progress is checked

Each level has a friendly checkpoint in week 6, a showcase and exit check in week 12, and a project rubric. Scores are used to decide what support to offer next. They are never grades. The rubric values three things equally: making the project your own, making it work, and being able to explain it. Rubric levels are Just starting, Getting there, Got it and Expert.

What you can celebrate: a working project at the end of each level, a child who can explain how it works, and a child who says "I found the bug".

Safety, privacy and inclusion

This is how the course keeps children safe:

  • No accounts, no logins, no email addresses.

  • Nicknames only; programs never ask for personal information.

  • Nothing is uploaded; projects stay on the computers in the room.

  • Screen breaks every session, plus unplugged activities.

  • Color-blind-safe materials and a dyslexia-friendly edition.

This website follows the same rules. It has no accounts, no analytics and no cookies; progress ticks stay in your own browser. See accessibility for the easy-read font and dark mode.

The three levels

  • Level 1: Introduction (Scratch → Python turtle). Final project: My Interactive Art Show. Notes for families.
  • Level 2: Intermediate (Python). Final project: Arcade Game or Art Studio. Notes for families.
  • Level 3: Advanced (Python projects). Final project: Build Something Big. Notes for families.
